description: User-facing project-agnostic safe-refactor refresher and bounded specialist dispatcher; it interprets current evidence and optional host support artifacts without owning implementation, delivery, validation, or snapshot/freeze writes.

support_artifact_roles.kanda_ast_safe_refactor_routine.py: current canonical read-only helper implementation support

human_ai_boundary: Human sets strategic direction and feature priority.
Human discusses implementation options before build.
Human confirms proposals before code is written or installed.
Human runs delivered install and validation commands and tests real behavior.
Human approves or rejects frozen-behavior changes.
AI proposes architecture, writes code, validators, and governed delivery artifacts.
AI does not ask the human to manually patch source as the normal implementation path.
do_not_regress: Keep this prompt a bounded user-facing refresher and specialist dispatcher, not a second governing refactor protocol.
When a host provides a Safe Refactor How To support-artifact bundle, keep the declared bundle bounded and keep worked examples explicitly non-authoritative.
Require exact current target evidence and never substitute historical examples for current source or audit truth.

Respect the active Project's module-size policy; when this prompt library's default is explicitly selected, keep the 400-line ideal and 500-line hard maximum and do not restore a universal 101-line minimum.

Delegate implementation admission to the active Project's declared authority, generic decomposition to KPR-06-007 when this library is present, and delivery/snapshot/freeze mechanics to current Project or host-specific owners.
Do not mutate host-specific planner, workbench, analysis queues, snapshot/freeze state, or target queues from the refresher itself.
